900100.title: The Lightning Bracket
900100.description: Sixty seconds per match: the fastest bracket in trivia.
900100.content:
The Lightning Bracket — Sixty seconds per match: the fastest bracket in trivia.

The lightning bracket compresses the tournament into pure adrenaline: each head-to-head match is sixty seconds, one question at a time, sudden death on the first miss. The format's genius is the clock as the opponent — solvers don't just battle each other, they battle the ticking. The hosting craft is the question pipeline: a stack of calibrated one-answer questions, read fast, judged instantly, no disputes entertained. The player skill is the quick recall — deep knowledge matters less than fast retrieval. The lightning bracket's crowd value is unmatched: every match is a minute of theater. Sixty seconds; one survivor.

Key points:
- Sixty-second sudden-death matches.
- The clock is the real opponent.
- Calibrated one-answer question pipeline.
- Every match is a minute of theater.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Lightning Bracket

900101.title: The Relay Question
900101.description: Pass the question down the line: the team relay round.
900101.content:
The Relay Question — Pass the question down the line: the team relay round.

The relay question turns a team into a chain: the question passes down the line, each player adding what they know, until the captain locks the answer. The design rule is the knowledge spread — the question must have layers (the era, the detail, the name) so different players contribute different pieces. The strategy is the order: put the broad-knowledge player first to frame it, the specialist last to nail it. The failure mode is the hog — one player answering everything while the team watches. The relay's lesson is collaboration made visible: the answer belongs to the chain, not the star. The team that relays together wins together.

Key points:
- Layered questions let everyone contribute.
- Order the chain: framer first, specialist last.
- Ban the hog: the chain answers.
- The answer belongs to the team.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Relay Question

900102.title: The Auction Round
900102.description: Bid your points on your confidence: the auction mechanic.
900102.content:
The Auction Round — Bid your points on your confidence: the auction mechanic.

The auction round lets teams bid points on questions: hear the category, bid what it's worth to you, then answer — right doubles the bid, wrong loses it. The mechanic's beauty is the confidence market: teams must price their own knowledge honestly. The strategy is the portfolio: bid big on your strengths, pass on your gaps, and watch rivals overpay for categories they half-know. The hosting craft is the category reveal — just enough information to tempt, never enough to be sure. The auction's drama is the all-in: a trailing team betting everything on one question. The auction round teaches the meta-skill of trivia: knowing what you know. Bid your confidence.

Key points:
- Bid points on your own confidence.
- Right doubles; wrong loses the bid.
- Portfolio strategy: big on strengths.
- Knowing what you know is the skill.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Auction Round

900103.title: The Streak Bonus
900103.description: Reward the hot hand: streaks that compound.
900103.content:
The Streak Bonus — Reward the hot hand: streaks that compound.

The streak bonus rewards consecutive correct answers with compounding points: two in a row doubles, three triples, and the room starts counting along. The psychology is the hot hand — teams play looser and sharper when the streak is alive, and the crowd invests in keeping it going. The design balance is the streak cap: uncapped streaks let one runaway team lap the field, so the wise host caps the multiplier at five. The strategy is the streak protection: teams spend their lifelines to keep streaks alive, which is exactly the drama the format wants. The streak bonus's lesson is momentum: trivia, like sport, has tides. Ride the hot hand.

Key points:
- Compounding points for consecutive correct.
- Cap the multiplier to prevent runaways.
- Teams spend lifelines protecting streaks.
- Momentum is real; ride it.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Streak Bonus

900104.title: The Rivalry Trophy
900104.description: A prize with a history: the traveling trophy.
900104.content:
The Rivalry Trophy — A prize with a history: the traveling trophy.

The rivalry trophy is a physical prize that travels: the winning team keeps it until the next showdown, their name engraved beside the last champions. The trophy's power is lineage — every engraving is a chapter, and teams play for the story as much as the win. The design is the artifact: it should be distinctive, slightly absurd, and impossible to ignore on a shelf. The ceremony is the transfer — the old champions hand it over in front of the room, with speeches. The rivalry trophy's economics are pure belonging: nobody needs a trophy, but everybody wants their name on one. The trophy travels; the legend stays.

Key points:
- Traveling prize with engraved lineage.
- Distinctive, slightly absurd artifact.
- The transfer ceremony matters.
- Teams play for the story.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Rivalry Trophy

900105.title: The Halftime Puzzle
900105.description: The intermission is a game too: the halftime puzzle.
900105.content:
The Halftime Puzzle — The intermission is a game too: the halftime puzzle.

The halftime puzzle fills the break with a different game: a cryptic, a logic grid, or a picture round that teams work while the host tallies. The design purpose is the reset — it breaks the question-answer rhythm and lets trailing teams strategize. The format rule is the parallel track: it must be solvable without the host, on paper, at the table. The scoring is the bonus: halftime points are small but they keep every team engaged through the break. The halftime puzzle's craft is the difficulty sweet spot — finishable in fifteen minutes by a decent team. The break becomes a round. The show never stops.

Key points:
- A different game for the intermission.
- Solvable on paper, without the host.
- Small bonus points keep teams engaged.
- The break becomes a round.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Halftime Puzzle

900106.title: The Captain's Gambit
900106.description: One decision per night: the captain's power play.
900106.content:
The Captain's Gambit — One decision per night: the captain's power play.

The captain's gambit gives each team one power play per night: double-or-nothing on a chosen question, played by the captain's sole decision. The mechanic's tension is the timing — play it early on a strength, or save it for a desperate late comeback. The team dynamics are the real game: the captain must read the room, weigh the category, and commit while the team holds its breath. The hosting rule is the declaration: the gambit must be declared before the question is read, no take-backs. The gambit's drama is the reveal — the room goes quiet for one question. One decision; one night; one legend. The captain earns the armband.

Key points:
- One double-or-nothing per night.
- Declared before the question is read.
- Timing is the whole strategy.
- The room goes quiet for the gambit.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Captain's Gambit

900107.title: The Overtime Gauntlet
900107.description: Tied at the death: the sudden-death gauntlet.
900107.content:
The Overtime Gauntlet — Tied at the death: the sudden-death gauntlet.

The overtime gauntlet settles ties with escalating sudden death: tied teams face questions of rising difficulty, and the first miss loses. The format's fairness is the shared gauntlet — both teams get the same questions in the same order, so the tiebreak is pure. The hosting craft is the question ladder: prepare ten questions of strictly increasing difficulty, because the gauntlet must end. The crowd value is the ascent — every survived round raises the gasp. The gauntlet's lesson is that ties deserve theater, not coin flips. The champions should win on knowledge, in front of everyone. Sudden death; shared questions; one winner.

Key points:
- Shared questions in the same order.
- Prepare a ladder of rising difficulty.
- The ascent is the theater.
- Ties deserve knowledge, not coin flips.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Overtime Gauntlet

900108.title: The Season Standings
900108.description: Eight weeks, one champion: the league format.
900108.content:
The Season Standings — Eight weeks, one champion: the league format.

The season standings turn isolated quiz nights into a league: eight weeks of play, points accumulating, the champion crowned at the finale. The format's power is the narrative arc — rivalries develop, comebacks happen, and week six matters because of weeks one through five. The scoring design is the balance: weekly wins matter, but consistency is rewarded, so a team that never wins a night can still take the season. The administration is the spreadsheet: publish standings after every night, because the table is the story. The season's magic is the finale — the last night with everything on the line. Eight weeks; one table; one champion. The league makes legends.

Key points:
- Points accumulate across eight weeks.
- Reward consistency, not just nightly wins.
- Publish the table after every night.
- The finale carries the season's weight.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Season Standings

900109.title: The Showdown Playbook
900109.description: The complete manual: hosting a group showdown.
900109.content:
The Showdown Playbook — The complete manual: hosting a group showdown.

The showdown playbook is the complete manual: format selection, question sourcing, hosting script, scoring system, and dispute protocol in one document. The planning timeline runs eight weeks out (book the venue), four weeks (write the questions), one week (dry run), and show night (run the script). The hosting script is the show's spine — every transition, every rule explanation, every ceremony, written down. The emergency section covers the disasters: the tie, the dispute, the technical failure, the walkout. The playbook's philosophy is that great nights are manufactured, not lucky. Write the manual; run the manual; the show runs itself. The host is the playbook's first reader.

Key points:
- Eight-week planning timeline.
- Script every transition and ceremony.
- Emergency section covers the disasters.
- Great nights are manufactured.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Showdown Playbook

900110.title: The Oceans Round
900110.description: Seventy percent of Earth, one round of questions.
900110.content:
The Oceans Round — Seventy percent of Earth, one round of questions.

The oceans round dives into the planet's majority: trenches, currents, and the creatures of the deep. The question craft is the scale ladder — from the familiar (the Pacific is the largest) to the abyssal (the Mariana Trench's depth) to the strange (the immortal jellyfish). The round's structure runs surface to seafloor: geography first, then life, then exploration history. The memorable questions are the superlatives — the deepest, the longest current, the largest animal that ever lived. The oceans round's lesson is how little we know: we've mapped Mars better than our own seafloor. The deep is the last frontier, and it's on our own planet.

Key points:
- Scale ladder: familiar to abyssal.
- Structure: surface to seafloor.
- Superlatives make memorable questions.
- We've mapped Mars better than the seafloor.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Oceans Round

900111.title: The Bridges of the World
900111.description: Spans and stories: the great bridges round.
900111.content:
The Bridges of the World — Spans and stories: the great bridges round.

The bridges round spans engineering and history: the longest, the oldest, and the ones with stories. The question craft is the record book — longest span, tallest tower, oldest surviving — plus the human tales (the workers, the disasters, the openings). The round's structure runs by type: suspension, arch, cable-stayed, each with its champions. The visual questions work best: show the silhouette, name the bridge. The bridges round's deeper theme is connection — every bridge is an argument that two sides should meet. The engineering is the poetry. The span is the story.

Key points:
- Records plus human stories.
- Structure by bridge type.
- Silhouette questions for visuals.
- Every bridge argues two sides should meet.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Bridges of the World

900112.title: The Inventions Timeline
900112.description: Who invented what, and when: the timeline round.
900112.content:
The Inventions Timeline — Who invented what, and when: the timeline round.

The inventions timeline round orders human ingenuity: the printing press, the steam engine, the light bulb, the internet — but the craft is the controversy. The question design loves the disputed firsts: who really invented the telephone, the airplane, the radio. The round's structure is chronological, and the game is the ordering — put these five inventions in sequence. The teaching payoff is the pattern: inventions cluster, build on each other, and arrive when the conditions are ripe. The timeline round's lesson is that invention is rarely a lone genius — it's a crowd, converging. The timeline is the truth; the lone genius is the myth.

Key points:
- Chronological structure; ordering games.
- Disputed firsts make great questions.
- Inventions cluster and converge.
- The crowd invents; the genius gets the credit.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Inventions Timeline

900113.title: The Currency Round
900113.description: Money around the world: the currency quiz.
900113.content:
The Currency Round — Money around the world: the currency quiz.

The currency round spends across the globe: the yen, the euro, the naira, and the stories printed on the notes. The question craft is the triple play — the currency's name, the country's name, and the face on the bill. The round's structure runs by region, and the visual questions shine: show the banknote, name the country. The memorable questions are the oddities — the currencies named after weights, the ones with holes, the hyperinflation notes. The currency round's deeper theme is trust: every banknote is a promise the whole country agrees to believe. The money is paper; the belief is the economy.

Key points:
- Triple play: currency, country, face.
- Regional structure; banknote visuals.
- Oddities make memorable questions.
- Every banknote is a shared promise.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Currency Round

900114.title: The Deserts Round
900114.description: The dry places: deserts of the world.
900114.content:
The Deserts Round — The dry places: deserts of the world.

The deserts round crosses the dry places: the Sahara's scale, the Atacama's dryness, the Gobi's cold, and Antarctica's technicality. The question craft is the definition game — what counts as a desert surprises everyone, and the largest desert on Earth is a polar one. The round's structure runs by superlative: largest, driest, hottest, coldest. The life questions are the wonder — the creatures and plants that thrive where rain never comes. The deserts round's lesson is adaptation: life doesn't need comfort, it needs a niche. The dry places are full. The desert blooms.

Key points:
- Definition games: what counts surprises.
- Superlative structure.
- Adaptation stories are the wonder.
- Life needs a niche, not comfort.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Deserts Round

900115.title: The Nobel Round
900115.description: The prizes and the laureates: the Nobel quiz.
900115.content:
The Nobel Round — The prizes and the laureates: the Nobel quiz.

The Nobel round honors the prizes: the categories, the laureates, and the stories behind the medals. The question craft is the people — Curie (twice), Einstein (not for relativity), the youngest and oldest winners. The round's structure runs by prize, and the literature and peace questions balance the sciences. The memorable questions are the snubs and surprises — who never won, who declined, who won for the wrong reason. The Nobel round's deeper theme is the prize's shadow: the award shapes what science values. The medal is metal; the recognition is the currency. The prize defines the pursuit.

Key points:
- People questions: the laureates' stories.
- Structure by prize category.
- Snubs and surprises stick.
- The prize shapes what science values.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Nobel Round

900116.title: The Volcano Round
900116.content:
The Volcano Round — Fire mountains: the volcano quiz.

The volcano round erupts with the planet's fire mountains: Vesuvius, Krakatoa, Mauna Loa, and the supervolcanoes sleeping beneath. The question craft is the power scale — the Volcanic Explosivity Index turns eruptions into numbers teams can rank. The round's structure runs by type: shield, stratovolcano, caldera, each with its champion. The history questions are the drama — Pompeii, the year without a summer, the island that vanished. The volcano round's lesson is the planet's engine: the ground we trust is a thin crust over fire. The mountain breathes. Respect the mountain.

Key points:
- The VEI turns eruptions into rankable numbers.
- Structure by volcano type.
- Eruption histories are the drama.
- The crust is thin; the fire is patient.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Volcano Round

900117.title: The Alphabets Round
900117.description: Scripts of the world: the writing systems quiz.
900117.content:
The Alphabets Round — Scripts of the world: the writing systems quiz.

The alphabets round writes across the world's scripts: Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, and the beautiful outliers like Hangul and Cherokee. The question craft is the visual: show the script, name the language — or show the language, name the script's inventor. The round's structure runs by family, tracing the great script lineages from Phoenician roots. The memorable questions are the designed scripts — Hangul's scientific design, the Cherokee syllabary's lone inventor. The alphabets round's deeper theme is the technology of thought: writing is humanity's first information revolution. The script is the software; the mind is the hardware.

Key points:
- Visual questions: show script, name language.
- Trace the great script families.
- Designed scripts make great stories.
- Writing is the first information revolution.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Alphabets Round

900118.title: The Endangered Species Round
900118.description: The rarest lives: the conservation quiz.
900118.content:
The Endangered Species Round — The rarest lives: the conservation quiz.

The endangered species round counts the rarest lives: the vaquita, the Javan rhino, the kakapo, and the numbers that keep falling. The question craft is the census — how many remain is a question with a shrinking answer. The round's structure runs by threat: habitat loss, poaching, climate, each with its victims. The hope questions balance the grief — the species brought back, the reserves that work, the breeding programs that beat the odds. The endangered round's lesson is the ledger: every extinction is a book burned unread. The count is the call to action. Know the number; feel the weight.

Key points:
- Census questions with shrinking answers.
- Structure by threat type.
- Hope stories balance the grief.
- Every extinction is a book burned unread.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Endangered Species Round

900119.title: The Everything Finals
900119.description: The championship of everything: the ultimate round.
900119.content:
The Everything Finals — The championship of everything: the ultimate round.

The everything finals is the championship: the top teams, the hardest questions, and the whole world as the category. The format is the gauntlet — rounds across every domain, no strengths to hide behind, the deepest bench wins. The question craft is the pinnacle: each question should be answerable by the prepared and impossible for the lucky. The hosting is the ceremony — the finals deserve staging, an audience, and a trophy with weight. The finals' lesson is the everything ideal: the champion isn't the specialist but the generalist, the team that knows a little about everything. The world is the category. Know the world.

Key points:
- Gauntlet format across all domains.
- Questions for the prepared, not the lucky.
- Stage the finals like a ceremony.
- The generalist takes the crown.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Everything Finals

900120.title: The Elders' Memory Round
900120.description: The town's memory, quizzed: honoring elder knowledge.
900120.content:
The Elders' Memory Round — The town's memory, quizzed: honoring elder knowledge.

The elders' memory round turns the community's oldest stories into questions: the flood year, the factory's heyday, the mayor everyone remembers. The question craft is the interview — sit with the elders, record the stories, and turn memory into fair questions. The round's structure runs by decade, walking the town's history from the oldest memory forward. The hosting rule is the honor: the elders are guests of honor, their answers celebrated, their corrections welcomed live. The round's deeper gift is the archive: the questions become a record of what the town remembers. The elders are the library. Quiz the library.

Key points:
- Interview elders; turn memory into questions.
- Structure by decade.
- Honor the elders as guests.
- The questions become the town archive.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Elders' Memory Round

900121.title: The Newcomers' Map Quiz
900121.description: Learn the town by playing: the welcome quiz.
900121.content:
The Newcomers' Map Quiz — Learn the town by playing: the welcome quiz.

The newcomers' map quiz teaches the town through play: the street names, the landmarks, the local legends every resident should know. The question craft is the orientation — each question teaches a fact the newcomer will actually use. The round's structure is the walking tour: downtown, the neighborhoods, the outskirts, in quiz form. The hosting trick is the teams: mix newcomers with old-timers, so the quiz is also an introduction. The map quiz's gift is belonging: the newcomer who can answer leaves feeling like a local. The town is the textbook. The quiz is the welcome.

Key points:
- Every question teaches a usable fact.
- Structure as a walking tour.
- Mix newcomers with old-timers.
- The quiz is the welcome.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Newcomers' Map Quiz

900122.title: The Main Street History Hunt
900122.description: The storefronts remember: a history hunt quiz.
900122.content:
The Main Street History Hunt — The storefronts remember: a history hunt quiz.

The main street history hunt quizzes the street itself: the ghost signs, the cornerstone dates, the buildings that changed purposes. The question craft is the fieldwork — walk the street, photograph the details, and build questions from what the buildings say. The round's structure runs block by block, a quiz-shaped walking tour. The hosting can go mobile: teams walk with answer sheets, and the street is the question paper. The hunt's lesson is attention: the familiar street is full of unread text. The buildings remember. Read the street.

Key points:
- Fieldwork: photograph the street's details.
- Block-by-block quiz structure.
- Mobile hosting: the street is the paper.
- The familiar is full of unread text.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Main Street History Hunt

900123.title: The Community Cookbook Quiz
900123.description: Recipes as heritage: the food memory quiz.
900123.content:
The Community Cookbook Quiz — Recipes as heritage: the food memory quiz.

The community cookbook quiz serves heritage on a question card: the church supper classics, the festival foods, the recipes every family claims. The question craft is the potluck — collect the recipes first (the quiz writes itself), then quiz the origins and the makers. The round's structure runs by occasion: holidays, fundraisers, family tables. The hosting secret is the tasting: serve the dishes while quizzing them, and the room becomes a feast. The cookbook quiz's gift is the archive: the collected recipes outlive the night. The food is the memory. Taste the heritage.

Key points:
- Collect recipes first; quiz writes itself.
- Structure by occasion.
- Serve the dishes during the quiz.
- The recipes outlive the night.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Community Cookbook Quiz

900124.title: The Volunteer Roll Call
900124.description: Honoring the helpers: the service quiz.
900124.content:
The Volunteer Roll Call — Honoring the helpers: the service quiz.

The volunteer roll call quizzes the community's service: the food bank's founding, the coach's decades, the cleanup crew's tonnage. The question craft is the research — the organizations' histories are the question bank, and the volunteers are the answer key. The round's structure runs by cause, honoring each sector of service. The hosting rule is the celebration: every answer is a thank-you, and the volunteers in the room get their ovation. The roll call's deeper purpose is recruitment: the quiz shows what needs doing and who's doing it. The helpers are the heroes. Name the helpers.

Key points:
- Organizations' histories are the bank.
- Structure by cause.
- Every answer is a thank-you.
- The quiz recruits the next volunteers.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Volunteer Roll Call

900125.title: The Local Legends Night
900125.description: Bigfoot to the ballplayer: the legends quiz.
900125.content:
The Local Legends Night — Bigfoot to the ballplayer: the legends quiz.

The local legends night quizzes the town's mythology: the ghost in the theater, the championship team, the eccentric inventor, the unsolved mystery. The question craft is the legend triage — separate the documented from the delicious, and quiz both honestly. The round's structure runs by legend type: ghosts, heroes, oddities, mysteries. The hosting fun is the debate: let the room argue the legends between questions. The legends night's gift is the shared story: the town's myths are its identity, told aloud. The legends are the town's dreams. Dream together.

Key points:
- Triage: documented vs. delicious.
- Structure by legend type.
- Let the room debate between questions.
- Shared myths are shared identity.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Local Legends Night

900126.title: The Schoolyard Reunion Quiz
900126.description: The old school days, quizzed: the reunion round.
900126.content:
The Schoolyard Reunion Quiz — The old school days, quizzed: the reunion round.

The schoolyard reunion quiz reopens the old yearbooks: the teachers, the teams, the scandals, the songs. The question craft is the archive — yearbooks, newspapers, and alumni memories are the question bank. The round's structure runs by era, so every generation gets its questions. The hosting magic is the slideshow: project the photos while quizzing them, and the room time-travels. The reunion quiz's gift is the reconnection: the questions are excuses to remember together. The school days are the common ground. Remember together.

Key points:
- Yearbooks and alumni are the bank.
- Structure by era for every generation.
- Slideshow hosting: project the photos.
- The questions are excuses to remember.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Schoolyard Reunion Quiz

900127.title: The Community Garden Quiz
900127.content:
The Community Garden Quiz — Growing knowledge: the garden quiz.

The community garden quiz grows questions from the soil: the planting calendar, the compost chemistry, the pollinator census. The question craft is the season — quiz what's growing now, and the garden is the study guide. The round's structure runs by bed: vegetables, herbs, flowers, the compost corner. The hosting can go outdoors: quiz among the rows, with the plants as visual aids. The garden quiz's lesson is the local food web: the quiz teaches ecology by naming it. The garden is the classroom. The harvest is the prize.

Key points:
- Quiz what's growing now.
- Structure by garden bed.
- Host outdoors among the rows.
- The garden teaches ecology by naming.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Community Garden Quiz

900128.title: The Town Hall Showdown
900128.description: Civics as sport: the local government quiz.
900128.content:
The Town Hall Showdown — Civics as sport: the local government quiz.

The town hall showdown makes civics a sport: the council's history, the budget's shape, the zoning fights, the ballot measures. The question craft is the public record — meeting minutes and budgets are the question bank, and they're all public. The round's structure runs by branch: the council, the departments, the ballot. The hosting rule is the neutrality: the quiz informs, never campaigns. The showdown's deeper purpose is the informed voter: the quiz is civics education disguised as fun. The town hall is the people's house. Know the house.

Key points:
- Public records are the question bank.
- Structure by branch of government.
- Neutral hosting: inform, never campaign.
- The quiz is civics education.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Town Hall Showdown

900129.title: The Belonging Scoreboard
900129.description: Measuring what matters: did the quiz build community?
900129.content:
The Belonging Scoreboard — Measuring what matters: did the quiz build community?

The belonging scoreboard measures the quiz's real product: not the points, but the belonging. The metrics are the mingling — new connections made, newcomers returning, teams mixing across old lines. The measurement tools are simple: the headcount of returners, the survey of new friends, the photo of the mixed tables. The design feedback is the loop: if the same cliques sit together every week, the format needs mixing mechanics. The scoreboard's philosophy is that the community quiz has two scoreboards — the night's winner, and the town's weaving. The points fade; the belonging compounds. Keep both scores.

Key points:
- Measure mingling, not just points.
- Track returners and new connections.
- Mixing mechanics break up cliques.
- Belonging compounds; points fade.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Belonging Scoreboard

900130.title: The Perpetual League
900130.description: The league that never ends: perpetual play.
900130.content:
The Perpetual League — The league that never ends: perpetual play.

The perpetual league is trivia without a finish line: rolling standings, no season end, the game continues as long as players show up. The format's engine is the rolling window — only the last twelve weeks count, so newcomers can always climb and veterans can't coast. The hosting craft is the rhythm: the same night, the same time, forever, because perpetuity needs reliability. The player psychology is the infinite game: nobody plays to win the league, they play to keep playing. The perpetual league's lesson is Carse's distinction — finite players play to win; infinite players play to continue. The league never ends. That's the point.

Key points:
- Rolling twelve-week standings window.
- Same night, same time, forever.
- Infinite game: play to keep playing.
- The league never ends.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Perpetual League

900131.title: The Question Cascade
900131.description: One question births ten: the cascade method.
900131.content:
The Question Cascade — One question births ten: the cascade method.

The question cascade is the bank's reproduction method: every good question births ten variants — the inversion, the deeper cut, the lateral leap, the superlative. The craft is the variant grammar: change the ask (who to when), change the depth (name to explain), change the angle (fact to story). The quality control is the freshness test: the variant must be independently interesting, not a pale echo. The cascade's economics are exponential: one seed question becomes a family, a family becomes a round. The method's discipline is the pruning: kill the weak variants, keep the strong. The bank grows like a river delta. One question; ten children.

Key points:
- Variant grammar: ask, depth, angle.
- Variants must be independently interesting.
- Prune the weak; keep the strong.
- One seed becomes a family.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Question Cascade

900132.title: The Difficulty Thermostat
900132.description: Keeping the room in the zone: dynamic difficulty.
900132.content:
The Difficulty Thermostat — Keeping the room in the zone: dynamic difficulty.

The difficulty thermostat keeps the room in the flow zone: too easy and the room bores, too hard and it quits, so the host adjusts in real time. The instrument is the room read — the speed of answers, the groans, the energy — and the control is the question queue, ordered easy to hard with branches. The technique is the pivot: when the room stalls, drop to a gimme; when it cruises, jump to the stumper. The data version is the calibration log: record every question's solve rate and let the numbers set the thermostat. The thermostat's philosophy is the host's real job: not reading questions, but tuning the room. The room is the instrument. Tune it.

Key points:
- Read the room: speed, groans, energy.
- Pivot: gimmes when stalled, stumpers when cruising.
- Log solve rates; let data tune.
- The host tunes the room.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Difficulty Thermostat

900133.title: The Archive Dive
900133.description: Old questions, new life: mining the archive.
900133.content:
The Archive Dive — Old questions, new life: mining the archive.

The archive dive resurrects old questions: the bank's history is a mine, and the dive brings up gems the room has forgotten. The craft is the dormancy rule — a question needs a year of rest before its encore, so the answers have faded. The remix is the art: update the framing, add a new angle, and the old question feels new. The curation is the theme dive: pull all the ocean questions for ocean night, and the archive becomes a themed round. The dive's economics are the bank's compound interest: every question written pays dividends forever. The archive is not a graveyard; it's a cellar. Dive deep; drink well.

Key points:
- Dormancy rule: a year before encore.
- Remix framing for fresh feels.
- Theme dives curate the archive.
- The bank pays compound interest.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Archive Dive

900134.title: The Remix Tournament
900134.description: Old questions, new games: the remix bracket.
900134.content:
The Remix Tournament — Old questions, new games: the remix bracket.

The remix tournament plays old questions as new games: the bank's history becomes the tournament's raw material, remixed into formats the original never imagined. The formats are the fun — the auction, the relay, the wager — each transforming familiar questions into fresh contests. The design rule is the transformation test: the format must change the skill, not just repackage the ask. The hosting craft is the reveal: don't announce the remix until the questions land. The tournament's lesson is the bank's second life: questions are content, formats are games, and the combinations are endless. The old bank; the new game. Remix everything.

Key points:
- Old questions as new games.
- Formats must change the skill.
- Reveal the remix at game time.
- Content times formats equals endless.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Remix Tournament

900135.title: The Freshness Metric
900135.description: Measuring staleness: the bank's health score.
900135.content:
The Freshness Metric — Measuring staleness: the bank's health score.

The freshness metric scores the bank's health: what fraction of questions are fresh to the room, and how fast is the fresh stock depleting. The measurement is the exposure log — every question's last-asked date — and the metric is the fresh ratio. The management rule is the pipeline rate: write new questions at the rate the room consumes them, plus a margin. The warning signs are the groans of recognition: when the room knows the questions, the metric has failed. The metric's discipline is the writing habit: a little every week beats a binge every quarter. The bank is a living thing. Feed it fresh.

Key points:
- Exposure log tracks every question.
- Fresh ratio is the health score.
- Write at consumption rate plus margin.
- Feed the bank weekly.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Freshness Metric

900136.title: The Crowdsource Pipeline
900136.description: The room writes the bank: the contribution system.
900136.content:
The Crowdsource Pipeline — The room writes the bank: the contribution system.

The crowdsource pipeline turns players into writers: the room submits questions, the editors curate, and the bank grows from the community's curiosity. The system is the submission form — question, answer, source, difficulty guess — simple enough to complete at the table. The curation is the editorial: fact-check everything, tune the difficulty, and credit the writer when it's asked. The incentive is the glory: writers love hearing their question read aloud. The pipeline's quality secret is the volume: accept many, publish few, and the bank's standard holds. The room knows things the host doesn't. Harvest the room.

Key points:
- Simple submission form at the table.
- Editorial: fact-check and tune.
- Credit writers when asked.
- Accept many; publish few.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Crowdsource Pipeline

900137.title: The Evergreen Bank
900137.description: Questions that never age: the timeless core.
900137.content:
The Evergreen Bank — Questions that never age: the timeless core.

The evergreen bank is the timeless core: questions that stay fresh forever because their answers don't change — the capitals, the elements, the classics. The curation is the timelessness test: will this question be as good in ten years. The bank's structure is the canon: the evergreen core that every room should know, surrounded by the seasonal fresh. The maintenance is the audit: revisit the core annually and prune what's dated. The evergreen's value is the foundation: new players need the canon before the novelties. The timeless questions are the bank's bedrock. Build on bedrock.

Key points:
- Timelessness test: good in ten years.
- Canon core plus seasonal fresh.
- Annual audit prunes the dated.
- New players need the canon first.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Evergreen Bank

900138.title: The Infinite Rivalry
900138.description: The rivalry that never resolves: the eternal matchup.
900138.content:
The Infinite Rivalry — The rivalry that never resolves: the eternal matchup.

The infinite rivalry is the matchup that never resolves: two teams, evenly matched, meeting week after week with the score never settling. The format's fuel is the balance — the rivalry needs parity, so the host handicaps gently to keep it close. The narrative is the saga: the comebacks, the streaks, the disputed calls, remembered and retold. The hosting craft is the stage: give the rivalry its moment, the featured table, the announced matchup. The rivalry's gift to the room is the stakes: everyone watches when the rivals meet. The infinite game needs its characters. The rivalry is the story.

Key points:
- Parity fuels the rivalry; handicap gently.
- The saga: comebacks retold.
- Stage the matchup; announce it.
- Rivalries give the room its stakes.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Infinite Rivalry

900139.title: The Eternal Season
900139.description: The season that never crowns: playing for the play.
900139.content:
The Eternal Season — The season that never crowns: playing for the play.

The eternal season is the season that never crowns a champion: standings are kept, but the title is perpetually contested, because the point was never the trophy. The philosophy is the infinite game made explicit: the players gather to play, the playing is the prize, and the season is the excuse. The format's mechanics are the gentle ones — rolling standings, participation honors, the rivalry of the week. The hosting tone is the celebration: every night is opening night. The eternal season's lesson is the deepest one trivia teaches: the game is the community, and the community is the game. The season never ends. Neither does the belonging.

Key points:
- Standings without a final crown.
- The playing is the prize.
- Every night is opening night.
- The game is the community.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Eternal Season

JAH-TRIVIA-000070.title: The Lightning Bracket
JAH-TRIVIA-000070.description: Sixty seconds per match: the fastest bracket in trivia.
JAH-TRIVIA-000070.content:
The Lightning Bracket — Sixty seconds per match: the fastest bracket in trivia.

The lightning bracket compresses the tournament into pure adrenaline: each head-to-head match is sixty seconds, one question at a time, sudden death on the first miss. The format's genius is the clock as the opponent — solvers don't just battle each other, they battle the ticking. The hosting craft is the question pipeline: a stack of calibrated one-answer questions, read fast, judged instantly, no disputes entertained. The player skill is the quick recall — deep knowledge matters less than fast retrieval. The lightning bracket's crowd value is unmatched: every match is a minute of theater. Sixty seconds; one survivor.

Key points:
- Sixty-second sudden-death matches.
- The clock is the real opponent.
- Calibrated one-answer question pipeline.
- Every match is a minute of theater.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Lightning Bracket

JAH-TRIVIA-000071.title: The Relay Question
JAH-TRIVIA-000071.description: Pass the question down the line: the team relay round.
JAH-TRIVIA-000071.content:
The Relay Question — Pass the question down the line: the team relay round.

The relay question turns a team into a chain: the question passes down the line, each player adding what they know, until the captain locks the answer. The design rule is the knowledge spread — the question must have layers (the era, the detail, the name) so different players contribute different pieces. The strategy is the order: put the broad-knowledge player first to frame it, the specialist last to nail it. The failure mode is the hog — one player answering everything while the team watches. The relay's lesson is collaboration made visible: the answer belongs to the chain, not the star. The team that relays together wins together.

Key points:
- Layered questions let everyone contribute.
- Order the chain: framer first, specialist last.
- Ban the hog: the chain answers.
- The answer belongs to the team.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Relay Question

JAH-TRIVIA-000072.title: The Auction Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000072.description: Bid your points on your confidence: the auction mechanic.
JAH-TRIVIA-000072.content:
The Auction Round — Bid your points on your confidence: the auction mechanic.

The auction round lets teams bid points on questions: hear the category, bid what it's worth to you, then answer — right doubles the bid, wrong loses it. The mechanic's beauty is the confidence market: teams must price their own knowledge honestly. The strategy is the portfolio: bid big on your strengths, pass on your gaps, and watch rivals overpay for categories they half-know. The hosting craft is the category reveal — just enough information to tempt, never enough to be sure. The auction's drama is the all-in: a trailing team betting everything on one question. The auction round teaches the meta-skill of trivia: knowing what you know. Bid your confidence.

Key points:
- Bid points on your own confidence.
- Right doubles; wrong loses the bid.
- Portfolio strategy: big on strengths.
- Knowing what you know is the skill.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Auction Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000073.title: The Streak Bonus
JAH-TRIVIA-000073.description: Reward the hot hand: streaks that compound.
JAH-TRIVIA-000073.content:
The Streak Bonus — Reward the hot hand: streaks that compound.

The streak bonus rewards consecutive correct answers with compounding points: two in a row doubles, three triples, and the room starts counting along. The psychology is the hot hand — teams play looser and sharper when the streak is alive, and the crowd invests in keeping it going. The design balance is the streak cap: uncapped streaks let one runaway team lap the field, so the wise host caps the multiplier at five. The strategy is the streak protection: teams spend their lifelines to keep streaks alive, which is exactly the drama the format wants. The streak bonus's lesson is momentum: trivia, like sport, has tides. Ride the hot hand.

Key points:
- Compounding points for consecutive correct.
- Cap the multiplier to prevent runaways.
- Teams spend lifelines protecting streaks.
- Momentum is real; ride it.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Streak Bonus

JAH-TRIVIA-000074.title: The Rivalry Trophy
JAH-TRIVIA-000074.description: A prize with a history: the traveling trophy.
JAH-TRIVIA-000074.content:
The Rivalry Trophy — A prize with a history: the traveling trophy.

The rivalry trophy is a physical prize that travels: the winning team keeps it until the next showdown, their name engraved beside the last champions. The trophy's power is lineage — every engraving is a chapter, and teams play for the story as much as the win. The design is the artifact: it should be distinctive, slightly absurd, and impossible to ignore on a shelf. The ceremony is the transfer — the old champions hand it over in front of the room, with speeches. The rivalry trophy's economics are pure belonging: nobody needs a trophy, but everybody wants their name on one. The trophy travels; the legend stays.

Key points:
- Traveling prize with engraved lineage.
- Distinctive, slightly absurd artifact.
- The transfer ceremony matters.
- Teams play for the story.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Rivalry Trophy

JAH-TRIVIA-000075.title: The Halftime Puzzle
JAH-TRIVIA-000075.description: The intermission is a game too: the halftime puzzle.
JAH-TRIVIA-000075.content:
The Halftime Puzzle — The intermission is a game too: the halftime puzzle.

The halftime puzzle fills the break with a different game: a cryptic, a logic grid, or a picture round that teams work while the host tallies. The design purpose is the reset — it breaks the question-answer rhythm and lets trailing teams strategize. The format rule is the parallel track: it must be solvable without the host, on paper, at the table. The scoring is the bonus: halftime points are small but they keep every team engaged through the break. The halftime puzzle's craft is the difficulty sweet spot — finishable in fifteen minutes by a decent team. The break becomes a round. The show never stops.

Key points:
- A different game for the intermission.
- Solvable on paper, without the host.
- Small bonus points keep teams engaged.
- The break becomes a round.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Halftime Puzzle

JAH-TRIVIA-000076.title: The Captain's Gambit
JAH-TRIVIA-000076.description: One decision per night: the captain's power play.
JAH-TRIVIA-000076.content:
The Captain's Gambit — One decision per night: the captain's power play.

The captain's gambit gives each team one power play per night: double-or-nothing on a chosen question, played by the captain's sole decision. The mechanic's tension is the timing — play it early on a strength, or save it for a desperate late comeback. The team dynamics are the real game: the captain must read the room, weigh the category, and commit while the team holds its breath. The hosting rule is the declaration: the gambit must be declared before the question is read, no take-backs. The gambit's drama is the reveal — the room goes quiet for one question. One decision; one night; one legend. The captain earns the armband.

Key points:
- One double-or-nothing per night.
- Declared before the question is read.
- Timing is the whole strategy.
- The room goes quiet for the gambit.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Captain's Gambit

JAH-TRIVIA-000077.title: The Overtime Gauntlet
JAH-TRIVIA-000077.description: Tied at the death: the sudden-death gauntlet.
JAH-TRIVIA-000077.content:
The Overtime Gauntlet — Tied at the death: the sudden-death gauntlet.

The overtime gauntlet settles ties with escalating sudden death: tied teams face questions of rising difficulty, and the first miss loses. The format's fairness is the shared gauntlet — both teams get the same questions in the same order, so the tiebreak is pure. The hosting craft is the question ladder: prepare ten questions of strictly increasing difficulty, because the gauntlet must end. The crowd value is the ascent — every survived round raises the gasp. The gauntlet's lesson is that ties deserve theater, not coin flips. The champions should win on knowledge, in front of everyone. Sudden death; shared questions; one winner.

Key points:
- Shared questions in the same order.
- Prepare a ladder of rising difficulty.
- The ascent is the theater.
- Ties deserve knowledge, not coin flips.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Overtime Gauntlet

JAH-TRIVIA-000078.title: The Season Standings
JAH-TRIVIA-000078.description: Eight weeks, one champion: the league format.
JAH-TRIVIA-000078.content:
The Season Standings — Eight weeks, one champion: the league format.

The season standings turn isolated quiz nights into a league: eight weeks of play, points accumulating, the champion crowned at the finale. The format's power is the narrative arc — rivalries develop, comebacks happen, and week six matters because of weeks one through five. The scoring design is the balance: weekly wins matter, but consistency is rewarded, so a team that never wins a night can still take the season. The administration is the spreadsheet: publish standings after every night, because the table is the story. The season's magic is the finale — the last night with everything on the line. Eight weeks; one table; one champion. The league makes legends.

Key points:
- Points accumulate across eight weeks.
- Reward consistency, not just nightly wins.
- Publish the table after every night.
- The finale carries the season's weight.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Season Standings

JAH-TRIVIA-000079.title: The Showdown Playbook
JAH-TRIVIA-000079.description: The complete manual: hosting a group showdown.
JAH-TRIVIA-000079.content:
The Showdown Playbook — The complete manual: hosting a group showdown.

The showdown playbook is the complete manual: format selection, question sourcing, hosting script, scoring system, and dispute protocol in one document. The planning timeline runs eight weeks out (book the venue), four weeks (write the questions), one week (dry run), and show night (run the script). The hosting script is the show's spine — every transition, every rule explanation, every ceremony, written down. The emergency section covers the disasters: the tie, the dispute, the technical failure, the walkout. The playbook's philosophy is that great nights are manufactured, not lucky. Write the manual; run the manual; the show runs itself. The host is the playbook's first reader.

Key points:
- Eight-week planning timeline.
- Script every transition and ceremony.
- Emergency section covers the disasters.
- Great nights are manufactured.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Showdown Playbook

JAH-TRIVIA-000080.title: The Oceans Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000080.description: Seventy percent of Earth, one round of questions.
JAH-TRIVIA-000080.content:
The Oceans Round — Seventy percent of Earth, one round of questions.

The oceans round dives into the planet's majority: trenches, currents, and the creatures of the deep. The question craft is the scale ladder — from the familiar (the Pacific is the largest) to the abyssal (the Mariana Trench's depth) to the strange (the immortal jellyfish). The round's structure runs surface to seafloor: geography first, then life, then exploration history. The memorable questions are the superlatives — the deepest, the longest current, the largest animal that ever lived. The oceans round's lesson is how little we know: we've mapped Mars better than our own seafloor. The deep is the last frontier, and it's on our own planet.

Key points:
- Scale ladder: familiar to abyssal.
- Structure: surface to seafloor.
- Superlatives make memorable questions.
- We've mapped Mars better than the seafloor.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Oceans Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000081.title: The Bridges of the World
JAH-TRIVIA-000081.description: Spans and stories: the great bridges round.
JAH-TRIVIA-000081.content:
The Bridges of the World — Spans and stories: the great bridges round.

The bridges round spans engineering and history: the longest, the oldest, and the ones with stories. The question craft is the record book — longest span, tallest tower, oldest surviving — plus the human tales (the workers, the disasters, the openings). The round's structure runs by type: suspension, arch, cable-stayed, each with its champions. The visual questions work best: show the silhouette, name the bridge. The bridges round's deeper theme is connection — every bridge is an argument that two sides should meet. The engineering is the poetry. The span is the story.

Key points:
- Records plus human stories.
- Structure by bridge type.
- Silhouette questions for visuals.
- Every bridge argues two sides should meet.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Bridges of the World

JAH-TRIVIA-000082.title: The Inventions Timeline
JAH-TRIVIA-000082.description: Who invented what, and when: the timeline round.
JAH-TRIVIA-000082.content:
The Inventions Timeline — Who invented what, and when: the timeline round.

The inventions timeline round orders human ingenuity: the printing press, the steam engine, the light bulb, the internet — but the craft is the controversy. The question design loves the disputed firsts: who really invented the telephone, the airplane, the radio. The round's structure is chronological, and the game is the ordering — put these five inventions in sequence. The teaching payoff is the pattern: inventions cluster, build on each other, and arrive when the conditions are ripe. The timeline round's lesson is that invention is rarely a lone genius — it's a crowd, converging. The timeline is the truth; the lone genius is the myth.

Key points:
- Chronological structure; ordering games.
- Disputed firsts make great questions.
- Inventions cluster and converge.
- The crowd invents; the genius gets the credit.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Inventions Timeline

JAH-TRIVIA-000083.title: The Currency Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000083.description: Money around the world: the currency quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000083.content:
The Currency Round — Money around the world: the currency quiz.

The currency round spends across the globe: the yen, the euro, the naira, and the stories printed on the notes. The question craft is the triple play — the currency's name, the country's name, and the face on the bill. The round's structure runs by region, and the visual questions shine: show the banknote, name the country. The memorable questions are the oddities — the currencies named after weights, the ones with holes, the hyperinflation notes. The currency round's deeper theme is trust: every banknote is a promise the whole country agrees to believe. The money is paper; the belief is the economy.

Key points:
- Triple play: currency, country, face.
- Regional structure; banknote visuals.
- Oddities make memorable questions.
- Every banknote is a shared promise.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Currency Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000084.title: The Deserts Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000084.description: The dry places: deserts of the world.
JAH-TRIVIA-000084.content:
The Deserts Round — The dry places: deserts of the world.

The deserts round crosses the dry places: the Sahara's scale, the Atacama's dryness, the Gobi's cold, and Antarctica's technicality. The question craft is the definition game — what counts as a desert surprises everyone, and the largest desert on Earth is a polar one. The round's structure runs by superlative: largest, driest, hottest, coldest. The life questions are the wonder — the creatures and plants that thrive where rain never comes. The deserts round's lesson is adaptation: life doesn't need comfort, it needs a niche. The dry places are full. The desert blooms.

Key points:
- Definition games: what counts surprises.
- Superlative structure.
- Adaptation stories are the wonder.
- Life needs a niche, not comfort.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Deserts Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000085.title: The Nobel Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000085.description: The prizes and the laureates: the Nobel quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000085.content:
The Nobel Round — The prizes and the laureates: the Nobel quiz.

The Nobel round honors the prizes: the categories, the laureates, and the stories behind the medals. The question craft is the people — Curie (twice), Einstein (not for relativity), the youngest and oldest winners. The round's structure runs by prize, and the literature and peace questions balance the sciences. The memorable questions are the snubs and surprises — who never won, who declined, who won for the wrong reason. The Nobel round's deeper theme is the prize's shadow: the award shapes what science values. The medal is metal; the recognition is the currency. The prize defines the pursuit.

Key points:
- People questions: the laureates' stories.
- Structure by prize category.
- Snubs and surprises stick.
- The prize shapes what science values.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Nobel Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000086.title: The Volcano Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000086.content:
The Volcano Round — Fire mountains: the volcano quiz.

The volcano round erupts with the planet's fire mountains: Vesuvius, Krakatoa, Mauna Loa, and the supervolcanoes sleeping beneath. The question craft is the power scale — the Volcanic Explosivity Index turns eruptions into numbers teams can rank. The round's structure runs by type: shield, stratovolcano, caldera, each with its champion. The history questions are the drama — Pompeii, the year without a summer, the island that vanished. The volcano round's lesson is the planet's engine: the ground we trust is a thin crust over fire. The mountain breathes. Respect the mountain.

Key points:
- The VEI turns eruptions into rankable numbers.
- Structure by volcano type.
- Eruption histories are the drama.
- The crust is thin; the fire is patient.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Volcano Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000087.title: The Alphabets Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000087.description: Scripts of the world: the writing systems quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000087.content:
The Alphabets Round — Scripts of the world: the writing systems quiz.

The alphabets round writes across the world's scripts: Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, and the beautiful outliers like Hangul and Cherokee. The question craft is the visual: show the script, name the language — or show the language, name the script's inventor. The round's structure runs by family, tracing the great script lineages from Phoenician roots. The memorable questions are the designed scripts — Hangul's scientific design, the Cherokee syllabary's lone inventor. The alphabets round's deeper theme is the technology of thought: writing is humanity's first information revolution. The script is the software; the mind is the hardware.

Key points:
- Visual questions: show script, name language.
- Trace the great script families.
- Designed scripts make great stories.
- Writing is the first information revolution.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Alphabets Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000088.title: The Endangered Species Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000088.description: The rarest lives: the conservation quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000088.content:
The Endangered Species Round — The rarest lives: the conservation quiz.

The endangered species round counts the rarest lives: the vaquita, the Javan rhino, the kakapo, and the numbers that keep falling. The question craft is the census — how many remain is a question with a shrinking answer. The round's structure runs by threat: habitat loss, poaching, climate, each with its victims. The hope questions balance the grief — the species brought back, the reserves that work, the breeding programs that beat the odds. The endangered round's lesson is the ledger: every extinction is a book burned unread. The count is the call to action. Know the number; feel the weight.

Key points:
- Census questions with shrinking answers.
- Structure by threat type.
- Hope stories balance the grief.
- Every extinction is a book burned unread.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Endangered Species Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000089.title: The Everything Finals
JAH-TRIVIA-000089.description: The championship of everything: the ultimate round.
JAH-TRIVIA-000089.content:
The Everything Finals — The championship of everything: the ultimate round.

The everything finals is the championship: the top teams, the hardest questions, and the whole world as the category. The format is the gauntlet — rounds across every domain, no strengths to hide behind, the deepest bench wins. The question craft is the pinnacle: each question should be answerable by the prepared and impossible for the lucky. The hosting is the ceremony — the finals deserve staging, an audience, and a trophy with weight. The finals' lesson is the everything ideal: the champion isn't the specialist but the generalist, the team that knows a little about everything. The world is the category. Know the world.

Key points:
- Gauntlet format across all domains.
- Questions for the prepared, not the lucky.
- Stage the finals like a ceremony.
- The generalist takes the crown.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Everything Finals

JAH-TRIVIA-000090.title: The Elders' Memory Round
JAH-TRIVIA-000090.description: The town's memory, quizzed: honoring elder knowledge.
JAH-TRIVIA-000090.content:
The Elders' Memory Round — The town's memory, quizzed: honoring elder knowledge.

The elders' memory round turns the community's oldest stories into questions: the flood year, the factory's heyday, the mayor everyone remembers. The question craft is the interview — sit with the elders, record the stories, and turn memory into fair questions. The round's structure runs by decade, walking the town's history from the oldest memory forward. The hosting rule is the honor: the elders are guests of honor, their answers celebrated, their corrections welcomed live. The round's deeper gift is the archive: the questions become a record of what the town remembers. The elders are the library. Quiz the library.

Key points:
- Interview elders; turn memory into questions.
- Structure by decade.
- Honor the elders as guests.
- The questions become the town archive.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Elders' Memory Round

JAH-TRIVIA-000091.title: The Newcomers' Map Quiz
JAH-TRIVIA-000091.description: Learn the town by playing: the welcome quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000091.content:
The Newcomers' Map Quiz — Learn the town by playing: the welcome quiz.

The newcomers' map quiz teaches the town through play: the street names, the landmarks, the local legends every resident should know. The question craft is the orientation — each question teaches a fact the newcomer will actually use. The round's structure is the walking tour: downtown, the neighborhoods, the outskirts, in quiz form. The hosting trick is the teams: mix newcomers with old-timers, so the quiz is also an introduction. The map quiz's gift is belonging: the newcomer who can answer leaves feeling like a local. The town is the textbook. The quiz is the welcome.

Key points:
- Every question teaches a usable fact.
- Structure as a walking tour.
- Mix newcomers with old-timers.
- The quiz is the welcome.

JAH-TRIVIA-000092.title: The Main Street History Hunt
JAH-TRIVIA-000092.description: The storefronts remember: a history hunt quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000092.content:
The Main Street History Hunt — The storefronts remember: a history hunt quiz.

The main street history hunt quizzes the street itself: the ghost signs, the cornerstone dates, the buildings that changed purposes. The question craft is the fieldwork — walk the street, photograph the details, and build questions from what the buildings say. The round's structure runs block by block, a quiz-shaped walking tour. The hosting can go mobile: teams walk with answer sheets, and the street is the question paper. The hunt's lesson is attention: the familiar street is full of unread text. The buildings remember. Read the street.

- Block-by-block quiz structure.
- Mobile hosting: the street is the paper.
- The familiar is full of unread text.

JAH-TRIVIA-000093.title: The Community Cookbook Quiz
JAH-TRIVIA-000093.description: Recipes as heritage: the food memory quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000093.content:
The Community Cookbook Quiz — Recipes as heritage: the food memory quiz.

The community cookbook quiz serves heritage on a question card: the church supper classics, the festival foods, the recipes every family claims. The question craft is the potluck — collect the recipes first (the quiz writes itself), then quiz the origins and the makers. The round's structure runs by occasion: holidays, fundraisers, family tables. The hosting secret is the tasting: serve the dishes while quizzing them, and the room becomes a feast. The cookbook quiz's gift is the archive: the collected recipes outlive the night. The food is the memory. Taste the heritage.

Key points:
- Collect recipes first; quiz writes itself.
- Structure by occasion.
- Serve the dishes during the quiz.
- The recipes outlive the night.

JAH-TRIVIA-000094.title: The Volunteer Roll Call
JAH-TRIVIA-000094.description: Honoring the helpers: the service quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000094.content:
The Volunteer Roll Call — Honoring the helpers: the service quiz.

The volunteer roll call quizzes the community's service: the food bank's founding, the coach's decades, the cleanup crew's tonnage. The question craft is the research — the organizations' histories are the question bank, and the volunteers are the answer key. The round's structure runs by cause, honoring each sector of service. The hosting rule is the celebration: every answer is a thank-you, and the volunteers in the room get their ovation. The roll call's deeper purpose is recruitment: the quiz shows what needs doing and who's doing it. The helpers are the heroes. Name the helpers.

Key points:
- Organizations' histories are the bank.
- Structure by cause.
- Every answer is a thank-you.
- The quiz recruits the next volunteers.

JAH-TRIVIA-000095.title: The Local Legends Night
JAH-TRIVIA-000095.description: Bigfoot to the ballplayer: the legends quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000095.content:
The Local Legends Night — Bigfoot to the ballplayer: the legends quiz.

The local legends night quizzes the town's mythology: the ghost in the theater, the championship team, the eccentric inventor, the unsolved mystery. The question craft is the legend triage — separate the documented from the delicious, and quiz both honestly. The round's structure runs by legend type: ghosts, heroes, oddities, mysteries. The hosting fun is the debate: let the room argue the legends between questions. The legends night's gift is the shared story: the town's myths are its identity, told aloud. The legends are the town's dreams. Dream together.

- Structure by legend type.
- Let the room debate between questions.
- Shared myths are shared identity.

JAH-TRIVIA-000096.title: The Schoolyard Reunion Quiz
JAH-TRIVIA-000096.description: The old school days, quizzed: the reunion round.
JAH-TRIVIA-000096.content:
The Schoolyard Reunion Quiz — The old school days, quizzed: the reunion round.

The schoolyard reunion quiz reopens the old yearbooks: the teachers, the teams, the scandals, the songs. The question craft is the archive — yearbooks, newspapers, and alumni memories are the question bank. The round's structure runs by era, so every generation gets its questions. The hosting magic is the slideshow: project the photos while quizzing them, and the room time-travels. The reunion quiz's gift is the reconnection: the questions are excuses to remember together. The school days are the common ground. Remember together.

Key points:

- Slideshow hosting: project the photos.
- The questions are excuses to remember.

JAH-TRIVIA-000097.title: The Community Garden Quiz
JAH-TRIVIA-000097.content:
The Community Garden Quiz — Growing knowledge: the garden quiz.

The community garden quiz grows questions from the soil: the planting calendar, the compost chemistry, the pollinator census. The question craft is the season — quiz what's growing now, and the garden is the study guide. The round's structure runs by bed: vegetables, herbs, flowers, the compost corner. The hosting can go outdoors: quiz among the rows, with the plants as visual aids. The garden quiz's lesson is the local food web: the quiz teaches ecology by naming it. The garden is the classroom. The harvest is the prize.

JAH-TRIVIA-000098.title: The Town Hall Showdown
JAH-TRIVIA-000098.description: Civics as sport: the local government quiz.
JAH-TRIVIA-000098.content:
The Town Hall Showdown — Civics as sport: the local government quiz.

The town hall showdown makes civics a sport: the council's history, the budget's shape, the zoning fights, the ballot measures. The question craft is the public record — meeting minutes and budgets are the question bank, and they're all public. The round's structure runs by branch: the council, the departments, the ballot. The hosting rule is the neutrality: the quiz informs, never campaigns. The showdown's deeper purpose is the informed voter: the quiz is civics education disguised as fun. The town hall is the people's house. Know the house.

- Public records are the question bank.
- Structure by branch of government.
- Neutral hosting: inform, never campaign.
- The quiz is civics education.
